newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco stocks close slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: Morocco stocks close slightly higher.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange ended its two-hour session on Tuesday with a 0.40 percent increase led by the four stocks traded on the electronic system, a market analyst said.
The all-share index closed at 601.09 points, up from 598.64 points on Monday, he said.
"Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur, Fertilizer firm, oil refinery and steel mill accounted for the main chunk of the trade on the official market," a broker at ABN-AMRO Finance said.
The four stocks were introduced in electronic trading early March.
rose 16 dirhams to 578 dirhams with 9,033 shares traded.
jumped 48 dirhams to 299.5 dirhams with 3,671 shares exchanged. was up 15 dirhams to 547 dirhams with 3,629 shares.
was the most active share with 22,450 shares changing hands.

Market activity was disrupted on Tuesday as the stock exchange's new headquarters were inaugurated in presence of Crown Prince Mohamed. The trading session took place late in the afternoon instead of the usual morning session.
ONA Group, Morocco's largest private conglomerate, remained unchanged at 760 dirhams.
Its subsidiary Financiere Diwan also rose nine dirhams to close at 339 dirhams.
Volume on the official market totalled 111 million dirhams from 76.6 million on Monday.
Trade was made up 332 deals involving 103,612 shares valued at 97,637,731 dirhams and 23 deals involving 5,549 privatisation bonds (worth 13,428,660 dirhams.
The volume for the unofficial market stood at 44.2 million dirhams from 24.5 million on Monday.
